alt.title.message: {image, select, logo {Logo} hero {Hero image} section {Image in the {section} section} other {An image}} has no alt text
alt.title.note: the composer's checks panel; section is the name of an email's section in lower case (footer, 2 columns)

alt.tag.note: a short label on the canvas, next to the image

alt.detail: Images are off by default in Outlook and many corporate clients; alt text is what shows, and spam filters score image-only mail higher.

alt.fix.note: the button that saves the alt text written in the field beside it

size.near.message: {kb} KB of Gmail's 102 KB clipping limit
size.near.note: the email's HTML size, near the size where Gmail cuts it

size.over: {kb} KB is over Gmail's 102 KB clipping limit
size.detail: Gmail clips the message and hides the footer, including the unsubscribe link.

size.minify.message: Minify inline CSS · saves about {kb} KB

size.bulkOne.message: The {section} section is the bulk of it ({share, number, percent}).
size.bulkOne.note: after size.detail: which section makes up most of the size; share: 46%

size.bulkMany.message: The {count, plural, =2 {two} =3 {three} =4 {four} =5 {five} =6 {six} =7 {seven} =8 {eight} =9 {nine} =10 {ten} other {#}} {section} sections are the bulk of it ({share, number, percent}).
size.bulkMany.note: several sections of the same kind: The three text sections

size.bulkCards.message: {count, plural, =2 {Two} =3 {Three} =4 {Four} =5 {Five} =6 {Six} =7 {Seven} =8 {Eight} =9 {Nine} =10 {Ten} other {#}} {section}{css, select, yes { with inline CSS} other {}} are the bulk of it.
size.bulkCards.note: rows of cards: Four product cards with inline CSS are the bulk of it

size.removeRow.note: a button: the last row of cards

ratio.title.message: The email is {share, number, percent} image
ratio.title.note: share: 92% of the email is images

ratio.detail: Spam filters score image-heavy mail higher, and most of it disappears when images are off. Add text or use fewer images.
footer.both: No unsubscribe link or postal address in the body
footer.bothTag: No unsubscribe link or postal address
footer.address: No postal address in the footer
footer.unsubscribe: No unsubscribe link in the body
footer.detail: Headers are added automatically, but the visible link and address are required too.

liquid.title.note: problem: the template engine's own words, in English

liquid.titleLine.note: a personalization tag that doesn't parse, at a line of the subject, preheader or body; problem: the template engine's own words, in English

liquid.detail: Fix the personalization tag; a broken tag would print as text or stop the send.

unknownField.title.message: {token} isn't a contact field; it prints nothing

unknownField.detail: Check the spelling, or add a fallback such as | default: "…".
subject.missingDetail: Inbox lists show the subject first; write one before sending.
subject.spam: Subject trips {count, plural, one {# spam heuristic} other {# spam heuristics}}
plainText.title: The plain-text version is empty
plainText.detail: The email has no text, so the text/plain part is blank. Add a sentence that says what the images show.
link.emptyDetail: People will click it; point it at the page it promises.

link.blocklistTitle.message: {kind, select, button {Button} image {Image} nav {Menu link} social {Social link} other {Link}} links to {host}, listed on {lists}
link.blocklistTitle.note: kind: what the link is; host: a domain; lists: blocklist names, SURBL and Spamhaus DBL

link.blocklistDetail: Mail linking to a blocklisted domain gets filtered regardless of your reputation. Use a domain you control.

link.replaceWithDestination.note: a button: points a listed or shortened link at the page it redirects to, once that page is known to be clean

link.shortenerTitle.message: {kind, select, button {Button} image {Image} nav {Menu link} social {Social link} other {Link}} redirects through {host}, a URL shortener

link.shortenerDetail: Shortened links hide where they go; filters treat them as suspicious and many shortener domains are blocklisted. Link to the page directly.

link.brokenTitle.message: {kind, select, button {Button} image {Image} nav {Menu link} social {Social link} other {Link}} to {url} {status, select, 0 {doesn't respond} other {returns {status}}}
link.brokenTitle.note: status: the HTTP status the page answered with, 404

link.brokenDetail: People who click get an error page. Fix the address or remove the link.

link.unknownTitle.message: Couldn't check {count, plural, one {# link domain} other {# link domains}} on {lists}
link.unknownTitle.note: lists: blocklist names, Spamhaus DBL and SURBL

link.unknownDetail: {trouble, select, refused {The lists refused this server's DNS resolver; blocklist lookups need your own recursive resolver.} other {DNS didn't answer in time.}} Not knowing isn't the same as clean: Send Readiness looks them up again before the send.

unknownField.titleFallback.message: {token} isn't a contact field, so everyone gets “{fallback}”
unknownField.titleFallback.note: token: a personalization tag, {{ frist_name }}; fallback: what it prints instead

unknownField.fallbackDetail: The fallback hides the typo in previews but not from your readers. Check the spelling against the fields in the token menu.
